reference: Contract expectations are taken from Bash's documented type/help builtin behavior and uv's published synopsis in docs/packages.md and loadables/uv.c. There is no matching GNU CLI for this loadable: it is a frontend to a separately packaged upstream uv executable, which is not available as an isolated fixture dependency here. No operation result is represented as GNU parity.
coverage: Bash reports uv as a builtin in the candidate.
Bash short help exposes the documented uv [UV-ARGS ...] synopsis.
Deferred: child argument, exported-environment, and exit-status forwarding with a deterministic local stand-in.
Deferred: helper resolution after changing directories following load-time resolution.
Deferred: documented missing-helper status and diagnostic with a controlled package tree.
Deferred: child signal handling and 128+N exit mapping in an isolated disposable VM.
Deferred: a bounded upstream uv project operation against an isolated local fixture/index.
exclusions: No network access or real package repository is used.
The runner cannot install a uv stand-in at the loadable's fixed compiled-in /usr/lib/bash-os/libexec/uv/uv path or provide a disposable package root for the separately packaged executable.
Package installation and environment creation are not GNU/POSIX command-line behaviors; operational cases remain deferred until an isolated upstream executable and local-only fixture are available.

cases.purpose: Check the Bash metadata contract that the optional uv loadable registers as a builtin.
Check the documented short Bash help synopsis for the uv builtin.
Exercise argument forwarding (including empty and spaced words), exported-variable visibility, and child exit-status propagation without contacting a package index.
cases.reason: uv is an optional loadable absent from both qualified binaries: legacy/uv/builtin-type and short-help-synopsis are SKIP ('loadable is not present in the candidate binary') in final-static and final-dynamic. The helper resolves ../libexec/uv/uv beside a loaded uv.so (uv.c dladdr) or the compiled-in /usr/lib/bash-os/libexec/uv/uv, so a relative package root works once a uv.so artifact is in the payload and the dynamic build can `enable -f` it. The candidate under qualification cannot execute any uv operation.
